summary.tldr: Creates a Criminal Code offence for repeated or continuous controlling or coercive conduct that seriously affects a connected person.
what_it_does: Creates an offence for repeatedly or continuously using controlling or coercive conduct toward a connected person when the conduct has a significant impact on them.
Defines a significant impact as causing a fear of violence, a decline in physical or mental health, or alarm or distress that seriously affects day-to-day life.

Defines connected people as current or former spouses, common-law partners or dating partners, people who agreed to marry, household members, relatives, and people who share parental responsibilities for the same child under 18.
Provides a defence, for conduct said to affect health or daily life, if the accused was acting in the person's best interests and the conduct was reasonable in all the circumstances.
Sets the penalty at either an indictable offence with up to five years in prison or a summary conviction offence.
who_it_affects: Parents sharing care of a child
People accused under the Criminal Code
summary.background: The bill adds new sections after section 264 of the Criminal Code.
